exposure: Incidental findings on brain MRI (e.g., acute cerebral infarcts, punctate white matter lesions (PWMLs), caudothalamic subependymal cysts, intracranial haemorrhage, subdural haemorrhage (SDH))
outcome: Prevalence of incidental findings on term neonatal MRI
Neurodevelopmental outcome at 18 months (Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development III scores for language, cognitive, and motor scales)
cohort: The study participants were 500 asymptomatic term neonates with normal clinical examination, enrolled in the Developing Human Connectome Project (dHCP) study between 2015 and 2019.
finding: Incidental findings are common on brain MRI in asymptomatic term neonates (47%), and the majority are clinically insignificant, with neurodevelopment at 18 months generally within the normal range.
mod_finding: Subdural haemorrhage (SDH) and punctate white matter lesions (PWMLs) were more common in infants delivered with ventouse-assistance compared to other delivery methods.
